title: sa-engine observability: shared definitions of sae-obs/1 and sae-bench/1
description: Definitions used by the stream record schema and the bench schema: the timeline key, units, statistics blocks, engine snapshots. Version 1.0 of the specification (docs/en/obs-spec.md).

u32.description: Unsigned 32-bit value. 4294967295 (0xFFFFFFFF) is the 'not applicable' value in key fields.

name.description: A dotted lower-case name of a counter, gauge, event, pass or owner (sim.dropped_ms, va.dxt, sae.clock.rebase).

fence.description: A fence name: F0..F7, with an optional lower-case sub-fence letter (F3b, F6a).

node.description: A node id: client-1, server, bot-017.

key.description: The timeline key. t_us is session time in microseconds in the server clock domain (local clock when not connected); tick is the server tick T = floor(t_us / dt_s_us); sub is the client simulation sub-tick k; frame is the client frame counter. 4294967295 in tick, sub or frame means 'not applicable' (no tick grid, classic mode, a record of a process without frames).

tsrc.description: Where t_us comes from: server (a server-side record), est (client estimate, clock locked), est_unlocked (client estimate before the lock), local (not connected, local QPC).

fence_ms.description: Milliseconds spent in the callbacks of each fence during the frame (or the tick).

ms_stats.description: A short statistics block of a duration series, in milliseconds.

frame_stats.description: Frame-time statistics. The same block is the 'frames' member of a stats record (the v1 getEngineStats numbers) and of a bench stage (the satk-bench/1 numbers): n frames, avg/p50/p95/p99/p999/max frame time, FPS, 1 % low (FPS of the mean of the slowest 1 % of frames), q = the 0th..100th percentile.

game.description: The game clock as the engine reports it (not session time).

clock_ratio.description: Game milliseconds per real millisecond over the window.

snapshot.description: An engine snapshot: what getEngineStats() reports besides the frame statistics. Used by stats records and by the start/end snapshots of a bench stage.
